pinyin: Shì yǐ dà zhàng fū chǔ qí hòu,
literal_gloss: Therefore the fully grown person dwells in its thickness,
our_english: This is why the great person dwells in the thick, not the thin,

pinyin: bù jū qí bó;
literal_gloss: and does not reside in its thinness;
our_english: dwells in the substance, not the blossom.

pinyin: chǔ qí shí, bù jū qí huá.
literal_gloss: Dwells in its fruit, and does not reside in its flowery display.
our_english: They let go of what is out there and take what is here.

pinyin: Gù qù bǐ qǔ cǐ.
literal_gloss: Therefore rejects that and takes this.
our_english: They let go of what is out there and take what is here.

pinyin: Xī zhī dé yī zhě
literal_gloss: Of old (in the beginning), these are the things that obtained/connected to the One (一):
our_english: These received the one long ago:

pinyin: Tiān dé yī yǐ qīng
literal_gloss: Heaven obtained the One, and by it became clear/pure/transparent.
our_english: Sky received the one, and so became clear.

pinyin: Dì dé yī yǐ níng
literal_gloss: Earth obtained the One, and by it became tranquil/solid/stable.
our_english: Earth received the one, and so became settled.

pinyin: Shén dé yī yǐ líng
literal_gloss: The spirits (invisible forces) obtained the One, and by it became numinous/active/alive.
our_english: Spirit received the one, and so became numinous.

pinyin: Gǔ dé yī yǐ yíng
literal_gloss: The valleys obtained the One, and by it became full/replenished.
our_english: The valley received the one, and so became full.

pinyin: Wàn wù dé yī yǐ shēng
literal_gloss: The ten thousand things obtained the One, and by it came to life/were born.
our_english: The countless things received the one, and so came to life.

pinyin: Hóu wáng dé yī yǐ wéi tiān xià zhēn
literal_gloss: Sovereigns and kings obtained the One, and by it became the true standard/anchor for the world.
our_english: Rulers received the one, and so serve as the world's standard.

pinyin: Qí zhì zhī
literal_gloss: Pushing this to its logical conclusion:
our_english: Follow it through:

pinyin: Tiān wú yǐ qīng, jiāng kǒng liè
literal_gloss: If heaven lacked clarity, it would shatter/tear.
our_english: Sky with no way to be clear is likely to split.

pinyin: Dì wú yǐ níng, jiāng kǒng fā
literal_gloss: If earth lacked stability, it would quake/crumble.
our_english: Earth with no way to be settled is likely to burst.

pinyin: Shén wú yǐ líng, jiāng kǒng xiē
literal_gloss: If spirits lacked numinosity, they would dissipate/fade away.
our_english: Spirit with no way to be numinous is likely to cease.

pinyin: Gǔ wú yǐ yíng, jiāng kǒng jié
literal_gloss: If valleys lacked fullness, they would dry up/exhaust.
our_english: The valley with no way to be full is likely to run dry.

pinyin: Wàn wù wú yǐ shēng, jiāng kǒng miè
literal_gloss: If the ten thousand things lacked life, they would go extinct.
our_english: The countless things with no way to live are likely to die out.

pinyin: Hóu wáng wú yǐ guì gāo, jiāng kǒng jué
literal_gloss: If sovereigns lacked nobility and height (from the root), they would topple/fall.
our_english: Rulers with no way to be prized and high are likely to topple.

pinyin: Gù guì yǐ jiàn wéi běn
literal_gloss: Therefore, the noble/expensive takes the lowly/cheap as its root base (本 \- běn).
our_english: So the prized takes the cheap as its root,

pinyin: Gāo yǐ xià wéi jī
literal_gloss: The high takes the low as its foundation (基 \- jī)
our_english: and the high takes the low as its footing.

chinese: 是以侯王自謂孤、寡、不穀。
pinyin: Shì yǐ hóu wáng zì wèi gū, guǎ, bù gǔ
literal_gloss: This is why sovereigns and kings call themselves "orphaned," "widowed," and "unworthy/grainless."
our_english: This is why rulers call themselves orphaned, alone, and unworthy.

pinyin: Cǐ fēi yǐ jiàn wéi běn xié? Fēi hū?
literal_gloss: Is this not taking the lowly as the root? Is it not?
our_english: Is this not taking the cheap as the root? Is it not?

pinyin: Gù zhì shù yù wú yù
literal_gloss: Therefore, the highest praise is to have no praise. (Note: some texts translate this as "taking a chariot apart leaves no chariot," but "highest praise is no praise" fits the vanity metaphor better).
our_english: So reduce a cart to the count of its parts, and there is no cart.

pinyin: Bù yù lù lù rú yù
literal_gloss: Do not desire to chime and shine like polished jade,
our_english: Do not want to be gleaming like jade,

pinyin: Luò luò rú shí
literal_gloss: \[But rather\] clatter and remain rough like common stone.
our_english: or common like stone.

pinyin: Fǎn zhě dào zhī dòng
literal_gloss: Returning/Reversion ( Fǎn ) is the movement ( dòng ) of the Tao;
our_english: Returning is the Tao’s movement;

pinyin: Ruò zhě dào zhī yòng
literal_gloss: Weakness/Yielding ( Ruò ) is the function/application ( yòng ) of the Tao.
our_english: Yielding is the Tao’s use.

pinyin: Tiān xià wàn wù shēng yú yǒu
literal_gloss: The ten thousand things under heaven ( Wàn wù ) are born from Being/Presence ( Yǒu );
our_english: The countless things of the world are born from presence;

pinyin: Yǒu shēng yú wú
literal_gloss: Being/Presence ( Yǒu ) is born from Non-Being/The Void ( Wú ).
our_english: Presence is born from absence.

pinyin: Shàng shì wén dào, qín ér xíng zhī
literal_gloss: Top-tier scholars/users ( Shàng shì ) hear the Tao, diligently practice/execute it ( xíng zhī ).
our_english: Those highest in service hear the Tao and practice it with diligence. / Those middling in service hear the Tao and keep some, forget some.

pinyin: Zhōng shì wén dào, ruò cún ruo wáng
literal_gloss: Mid-tier scholars/users ( Zhōng shì ) hear the Tao, seemingly keep/preserve it ( cún ), seemingly lose/forget it ( wáng ).
our_english: Those lowest in service hear the Tao and laugh aloud at it. / If it weren’t laughed at, the Tao wouldn’t be what it is.

pinyin: Xià shì wén dào, dà xiào zhī
literal_gloss: Low-tier scholars/users ( Xià shì ) hear the Tao, laugh loudly at it.
our_english: Therefore, as the established sayings have it:

pinyin: Bù xiào bù zú yǐ wéi dào
literal_gloss: If it were not laughed at, it would not be sufficient ( zú ) to function as ( wéi ) the Tao.
our_english: The clear Tao seems murky. / The advancing Tao seems to retreat.

pinyin: Gù jiàn yán yǒu zhī:
literal_gloss: Therefore established sayings have it:
our_english: The level Tao seems rough.

chinese: 明道若昧，進道若退，夷道若纇。
pinyin: Míng dào ruò mèi, jìn dào ruò tuì, yí dào ruò lèi.
literal_gloss: The bright Tao seems dark/obscure, the advancing Tao seems to retreat, the level/smooth Tao seems rough/uneven.
our_english: The highest integrity seems a valley. / The whitest white seems soiled.

pinyin: Shàng dé ruò gǔ, dà bái ruò rǔ,
literal_gloss: Highest capacity/virtue seems like a valley, great white/purity seems disgraced/soiled.
our_english: Boundless integrity seems not enough. / Sturdy integrity seems slack.

chinese: 廣德若不足，建德若偷，質真若渝。
pinyin: Guǎng dé ruò bù zú, jiàn dé ruò tōu, zhì zhēn ruò yú.
literal_gloss: Broad capacity seems insufficient, established capacity seems stealthy/shirking, pure substance seems to fade/change.
our_english: Substantial truth seems to waver.

pinyin: Dà fāng wú yú, dà qì wǎn chéng,
literal_gloss: The great square has no corners, the great tool/vessel is late to compile/complete.
our_english: The great square has no corners. / The great vessel is never completed.

pinyin: Dà yīn xī shēng, dà xiàng wú xíng.
literal_gloss: The great sound has sparse sound, the great form/image has no shape.
our_english: The great sound is barely heard.

pinyin: Dào yǐn wú míng.
literal_gloss: The Tao is hidden and lacks a name/ledger.
our_english: The great image has no form. / The Tao is hidden and nameless.

pinyin: Fú wéi dào, shàn dài qiě chéng.
literal_gloss: Yet only the Tao is masterful ( Shàn ) at lending/initiating and compiling/completing ( Chéng ).
our_english: Only the Tao is masterful at lending, and at completing.

chinese: 道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。
pinyin: Dào shēng yī, yī shēng èr, èr shēng sān, sān shēng wàn wù.
literal_gloss: The Tao generates the One, the One generates the Two, the Two generates the Three, the Three generates the ten thousand things.
our_english: The Tao births the one, the one births the two, the two births the three, the three births the countless things.

chinese: 萬物負陰而抱陽，沖氣以為和。
pinyin: Wàn wù fù yīn ér bào yáng, chōng qì yǐ wéi hé.
literal_gloss: The ten thousand things carry Yin on their backs and embrace Yang, blending the vital breath (qi) to achieve harmony.
our_english: The countless things carry yin on their backs and embrace yang with their arms, blending the vital breath into harmony.

pinyin: Rén zhī suǒ wù, wéi gū, guǎ, bù gǔ,
literal_gloss: What people despise are 'orphaned,' 'widowed,' and 'unworthy/grainless',
our_english: What most people hate is to be called orphaned, meager, or unworthy,

pinyin: ér wáng gōng yǐ wéi chēng.
literal_gloss: yet kings and dukes use these as their titles.
our_english: Yet rulers and lords take these very descriptions for themselves.

chinese: 故物或損之而益，或益之而損。
pinyin: Gù wù huò sǔn zhī ér yì, huò yì zhī ér sǔn.
literal_gloss: Therefore, things might be diminished and yet increase, or be increased and yet diminish.
our_english: For so it is: what is decreased is thereby increased, and what is increased is thereby decreased.

pinyin: Rén zhī suǒ jiào, wǒ yì jiào zhī.
literal_gloss: What others teach, I also teach.
our_english: What others teach, I also teach:

pinyin: Qiáng liáng zhě bù dé qí sǐ,
literal_gloss: The violent and rigid do not meet their natural death,
our_english: The strong and rigid do not die a natural death.

pinyin: Wú jiāng yǐ wéi jiào fù.
literal_gloss: I will take this as the father of my teaching.
our_english: I take this as the root of learning.

chinese: 天下之至柔，馳騁天下之至堅。
pinyin: Tiān xià zhī zhì róu, chí chěng tiān xià zhī zhì jiān.
literal_gloss: The softest thing in the world dashes/gallops through the hardest thing in the world.
our_english: The softest thing in the world gallops over the hardest thing in the world.

pinyin: Wú yǒu rù wú jiàn,
literal_gloss: That which has no physical presence (wu you) enters where there is no space/gap (wu jian),
our_english: The formless enters the seamless.

pinyin: Wú shì yǐ zhī wú wéi zhī yǒu yì.
literal_gloss: Therefore I know the benefit/advantage of zero-friction execution (wu wei).
our_english: This is how I know the benefit of non-doing.

pinyin: Bù yán zhī jiào, wú wéi zhī yì,
literal_gloss: The teaching without words, the benefit of zero-friction execution,
our_english: The wordless teaching, the benefit of non-doing —

pinyin: Tiān xià xī jí zhī.
literal_gloss: few in the world can reach/match it.
our_english: few ever reach this.

pinyin: Míng yǔ shēn shú qīn?
literal_gloss: Fame/Name or the body/self, which is closer/dearer?
our_english: Reputation or your body — which is dearer?

pinyin: Shēn yǔ huò shú duō?
literal_gloss: The body/self or wealth/goods, which is more/worth more?
our_english: Your body or goods — which is worth more?

pinyin: Dé yǔ wáng shú bìng?
literal_gloss: Gaining or losing, which is the disease/harm?
our_english: Gain or loss — which does more harm?

pinyin: Shì gù shèn ài bì dà fèi,
literal_gloss: Therefore, extreme love/attachment must lead to great expenditure/waste,
our_english: Therefore, extreme attachment inevitably brings great cost

pinyin: Duō cáng bì hòu wáng.
literal_gloss: Heavy hoarding must lead to massive loss.
our_english: And hoarding inevitably brings heavy loss.

pinyin: Zhī zú bù rǔ,
literal_gloss: Knowing sufficiency/enough, one avoids disgrace,
our_english: Know when you have enough, and you are never disgraced.

pinyin: Zhī zhǐ bù dài,
literal_gloss: Knowing when to stop, one avoids danger/exhaustion,
our_english: Know when to stop, and you come to no danger.

pinyin: Kě yǐ cháng jiǔ.
literal_gloss: Thus one can endure long.
our_english: And so you can last long.

pinyin: Dà chéng ruò quē, qí yòng bù bì.
literal_gloss: Great perfection/compilation seems flawed/lacking, yet its function/utility is never impaired.
our_english: Great completeness seems deficient, yet when used, it never wears out.

pinyin: Dà yíng ruò chōng, qí yòng bù qióng.
literal_gloss: Great fullness seems empty/hollow, yet its function/utility is never exhausted.
our_english: Great fullness seems empty, yet when used, it never runs dry.

pinyin: Dà zhí ruò qū,
literal_gloss: Great straightness seems bent/crooked,
our_english: Great straightness seems crooked.

pinyin: Dà qiǎo ruò zhuō,
literal_gloss: Great skill seems clumsy/clunky,
our_english: Great skill seems clumsy.

pinyin: Dà biàn ruò nè.
literal_gloss: Great eloquence seems stuttering/awkward.
our_english: Great argument seems halting.

pinyin: Zào shèng hán, jìng shèng rè.
literal_gloss: Agitation/Movement overcomes cold, stillness overcomes heat.
our_english: Movement overcomes cold; stillness overcomes heat.

pinyin: Qīng jìng wéi tiān xià zhèng.
literal_gloss: Clarity and stillness function as the standard/ruler for the world.
our_english: Clear stillness brings order to the world.

pinyin: Tiān xià yǒu dào, què zǒu mǎ yǐ fèn.
literal_gloss: When the world has the Tao, swift horses are retired to fertilize fields with their dung.
our_english: When the world embraces the Tao, swift horses are retired to work the fields.

pinyin: Tiān xià wú dào, róng mǎ shēng yú jiāo.
literal_gloss: When the world lacks the Tao, war horses are bred in the suburbs/borders.
our_english: When the world lacks the Tao, war horses are bred in the borderlands.

pinyin: Huò mò dà yú bù zhī zú;
literal_gloss: There is no disaster greater than not knowing sufficiency.
our_english: There is no greater disaster than discontent,

pinyin: Jiù mò dà yú yù dé.
literal_gloss: There is no fault/flaw greater than the desire to acquire.
our_english: No greater fault than craving to acquire.

pinyin: Gù zhī zú zhī zú, cháng zú yǐ.
literal_gloss: Therefore, the sufficiency of knowing sufficiency is eternally sufficient.
our_english: And so the contentment of knowing you have enough is ever-present contentment.

pinyin: Bù chū hù, zhī tiān xià;
literal_gloss: Without going out the door, one can know the world;
our_english: Without leaving home, you know the whole world. / Without looking out the window, you see the way of nature.

pinyin: Bù kuī yǒu, jiàn tiān dào.
literal_gloss: Without looking through the window, one can see the Tao of heaven.
our_english: The further out you venture, the less you know.

pinyin: Qí chū mí yuǎn, qí zhī mí shǎo.
literal_gloss: The further one goes out, the less one knows.
our_english: Therefore, the sage knows without venturing,

pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén bù xíng ér zhī,
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage knows without traveling,
our_english: understands clearly without seeing,

pinyin: Bù jiàn ér míng, bù wéi ér chéng.
literal_gloss: understands/sees clearly without looking, compiles/completes without forcing action.
our_english: and accomplishes without acting.

pinyin: Wéi xué rì yì, wéi dào rì sǔn.
literal_gloss: Pursuing study/learning, one increases daily; pursuing the Tao, one decreases daily.
our_english: In pursuit of learning, you increase daily; / in pursuit of the Tao, you decrease daily.

pinyin: Sǔn zhī yòu sǔn, yǐ zhì yú wú wéi.
literal_gloss: Decreasing and decreasing again, until reaching zero-friction execution (wu wei).
our_english: Decreasing and decreasing, until you reach non-doing.

pinyin: Wú wéi ér wú bù wéi.
literal_gloss: Zero-friction execution, yet nothing is left undone/unexecuted.
our_english: Non-doing, yet nothing is left undone.

pinyin: Qǔ tiān xià cháng yǐ wú shì,
literal_gloss: Taking (qu) the world is always (chang) by means of no-undertaking (wu shi),
our_english: The world always comes to you by not meddling with it.

chinese: 及其有事，不足以取天下。
pinyin: Jí qí yǒu shì, bù zú yǐ qǔ tiān xià.
literal_gloss: Once there is undertaking (you shi), that is not enough (bu zu) to take the world.
our_english: The moment you meddle, it stops coming.

chinese: 聖人無常心，以百姓心為心。
pinyin: Shèng rén wú cháng xīn, yǐ bǎi xìng xīn wéi xīn.
literal_gloss: The Sage has no constant/fixed mind, takes the people's mind as their mind.
our_english: The sage has no fixed heart; / they take the heart of the people as their own.

pinyin: Shàn zhě, wú shàn zhī;
literal_gloss: The masterful ones (shan zhe), I count as masterful (shan zhi — shan used as a verb, "to reckon as shan");
our_english: The masterful, I count as masterful;

pinyin: Bù shàn zhě, wú yì shàn zhī;
literal_gloss: The unmasterful, I also (yi) count as masterful;
our_english: the unmasterful, I count as masterful too.

pinyin: Dé shàn.
literal_gloss: Integrity (de) is mastery (shan). Two characters, no verb and no causal word.
our_english: Integrity is mastery. / The trustworthy, I trust;

pinyin: Xìn zhě, wú xìn zhī;
literal_gloss: Those who are reliable/trustworthy, I trust/rely on;
our_english: the untrustworthy, I trust as well.

pinyin: Bù xìn zhě, wú yì xìn zhī;
literal_gloss: Those who are unreliable/untrustworthy, I also trust/rely on;
our_english: Integrity is trust.

pinyin: Dé xìn.
literal_gloss: Integrity is trust (xin).
our_english: In the world, the sage breathes gently; / for the sake of the world, they let their heart go muddy.

chinese: 聖人在天下，歙歙焉，為天下渾其心，
pinyin: Shèng rén zài tiān xià, xī xī yān, wéi tiān xià hún qí xīn,
literal_gloss: The sage in the world breathes gently (xi xi — to draw in); for the sake of the world, muddies (hun) their heart (xin).
our_english: The people pour out their attention, all eyes and ears;

chinese: 百姓皆注其耳目，聖人皆孩之。
pinyin: Bǎi xìng jiē zhù qí ěr mù, shèng rén jiē hái zhī.
literal_gloss: The people all pour (zhu) their ears and eyes; the sage sees them all as hai (an infant — the Shuowen glosses its older form as "a small child's laugh").
our_english: the sage sees them pure as infants.

pinyin: Chū shēng rù sǐ.
literal_gloss: Emerge into life, enter into death.
our_english: Emerge into life, enter into death.

pinyin: Shēng zhī tú, shí yǒu sān;
literal_gloss: The followers of life are three in ten;
our_english: Three in ten people are followers of life.

pinyin: Sǐ zhī tú, shí yǒu sān;
literal_gloss: The followers of death are three in ten;
our_english: Three in ten are followers of death.

chinese: 人之生，動之於死地，亦十有三。
pinyin: Rén zhī shēng, dòng zhī yú sǐ dì, yì shí yǒu sān.
literal_gloss: People whose lives move them toward the realm of death are also three in ten.
our_english: Three in ten, though alive, move toward deadly ground.

pinyin: Fú hé gù? Yǐ qí shēng shēng zhī hòu.
literal_gloss: For what reason? Because they live their lives too thickly (with excessive attachment).
our_english: Why? Because they cling too tightly to life.

pinyin: Gài wén shàn shè shēng zhě,
literal_gloss: It has been said that one who is expert at preserving life,
our_english: It’s been said that one who truly tends life

pinyin: Lù xíng bù yù sì hǔ,
literal_gloss: Traveling on land, does not encounter rhinos or tigers,
our_english: can travel the land without meeting rhinos or tigers,

pinyin: Rù jūn bù pèi jiǎ bīng;
literal_gloss: Entering an army/battle, is not touched by armor or weapons;
our_english: and can enter into battle unharmed by weapons.

pinyin: Sì wú suǒ tóu qí jiǎo,
literal_gloss: The rhino has nowhere to thrust its horn,
our_english: The rhino’s horn has nowhere to thrust,

pinyin: Hǔ wú suǒ yòng qí zhǎo,
literal_gloss: The tiger has nowhere to use its claws,
our_english: the tiger’s claws have nowhere to tear into,

pinyin: Bīng wú suǒ róng qí rèn.
literal_gloss: The weapon has nowhere to house its blade.
our_english: the weapon blades have nothing to cut.

pinyin: Fú hé gù? Yǐ qí wú sǐ dì.
literal_gloss: For what reason? Because in them there is no realm of death (no fatal vulnerability).
our_english: Why? Because they give death no foothold.

pinyin: Dào shēng zhī, dé xù zhī,
literal_gloss: The Tao generates them, the Te/Virtue nourishes them,
our_english: The Tao gives birth to the countless things, integrity rears them, / matter forms them, circumstance completes them.

pinyin: Wù xíng zhī, shì chéng zhī.
literal_gloss: Matter/Physical entities give them form, momentum/circumstance completes/compiles them.
our_english: Therefore the countless things, without exception, revere the Tao and value integrity.

chinese: 是以萬物莫不尊道而貴德。
pinyin: Shì yǐ wàn wù mò bù zūn dào ér guì dé.
literal_gloss: Therefore the ten thousand things cannot but revere the Tao and value the Te.
our_english: This reverence for the Tao, this valuing of integrity — no one commands it.

pinyin: Dào zhī zūn, dé zhī guì,
literal_gloss: The reverence for the Tao, the valuing of the Te,
our_english: It is always so, of itself.

pinyin: Fú mò zhī mìng ér cháng zì rán.
literal_gloss: Is not commanded/ordered by anyone, but is eternally spontaneous/autonomous (zi ran).
our_english: Thus, the Tao births the countless things and integrity rears them, / grows and raises them, settles and matures them, nourishes and protects them.

pinyin: Gù dào shēng zhī, dé xù zhī;
literal_gloss: Therefore the Tao generates them, the Te nourishes them;
our_english: Giving birth without possessing,

chinese: 長之育之；亭之毒之；養之覆之。
pinyin: Zhǎng zhī yù zhī; tíng zhī dú zhī; yǎng zhī fù zhī.
literal_gloss: Grows them, rears them; shapes them, matures them; sustains them, covers/protects them.
our_english: acting yet relying on nothing,

chinese: 生而不有，為而不恃，長而不宰。
pinyin: Shēng ér bù yǒu, wéi ér bù shì, zhǎng ér bù zǎi.
literal_gloss: Generating but not possessing/owning, executing/acting but not depending/relying, growing/leading but not dominating/ruling.
our_english: growing them without ruling them –

pinyin: Shì wèi xuán dé.
literal_gloss: This is called Profound/Dark Virtue (Te).
our_english: this is called profound integrity.

pinyin: Tiān xià yǒu shǐ, yǐ wéi tiān xià mǔ.
literal_gloss: The world has a beginning, which serves as the mother of the world.
our_english: The world has an origin, which serves as the mother of the world. / Find our mother, and you know her children.

pinyin: Jì dé qí mǔ, yǐ zhī qí zǐ;
literal_gloss: Having obtained/known the mother, one thereby knows the children/offspring;
our_english: Know her children, return and hold fast to our mother,

chinese: 既知其子，復守其母，没身不殆。
pinyin: Jì zhī qí zǐ, fù shǒu qí mǔ, mò shēn bù dài.
literal_gloss: Having known the children, returning to guard the mother, to the end of one's life there is no danger.
our_english: and to the end of your days, no danger will find you. / Block the openings, close the doors, and to the end of your days you will not toil.

chinese: 塞其兌，閉其門，終身不勤。
pinyin: Sè qí duì, bì qí mén, zhōng shēn bù qín.
literal_gloss: Block the openings, close the doors, to the end of life one does not toil/struggle.
our_english: Open the openings, multiply your affairs, and to the end of your days you are beyond saving.

chinese: 開其兌，濟其事，終身不救。
pinyin: Kāi qí duì, ji qí shì, zhōng shēn bù jiù.
literal_gloss: Open the openings, multiply affairs/tasks, to the end of life one is beyond rescue.
our_english: To recognize things in their smallest form is clear-seeing.

pinyin: Jiàn xiǎo yuē míng, shǒu róu yuē qiáng.
literal_gloss: Seeing the small is called clarity/illumination, guarding the soft/yielding is called strength.
our_english: Holding to the soft is called strong. / Use the outer light, return to your inner clarity,

chinese: 用其光，復歸其明，無遺身殃；
pinyin: Yòng qí guāng, fù guī qí míng, wú yí shēn yāng;
literal_gloss: Use the light, return to the clarity/illumination, leaving no disaster for the body;
our_english: and leave no calamity for the body.

pinyin: Shì wèi xí cháng.
literal_gloss: This is called inheriting/practicing the constant.
our_english: This is called the ever-present worn covered.

chinese: 使我介然有知，行於大道，唯施是畏。
pinyin: Shǐ wǒ jiè rán yǒu zhī, xíng yú dà dào, wéi shī shì wèi.
literal_gloss: If I had just a little knowledge, walking on the Great Tao, my only fear would be straying/deviating from it.
our_english: If I had just a scrap of knowledge, walking the path of the great Tao, my only fear would be to stray from it.

pinyin: Dà dào shèn yí, ér rén hào jìng.
literal_gloss: The Great Tao is very level/smooth, yet people love the bypaths/shortcuts.
our_english: The great Tao is very level, yet people love to take shortcuts.

pinyin: Cháo shèn chú, tián shèn wú, cāng shèn xū;
literal_gloss: The courts are highly maintained/clean, the fields are overgrown with weeds, the granaries are completely empty;
our_english: The courts are immaculate, the fields are choked with weeds, the granaries are empty;

chinese: 服文綵，帶利劍，厭飲食，財貨有餘；
pinyin: Fú wén cǎi, dài lì jiàn, yàn yǐn shí, cái huò yǒu yú;
literal_gloss: Wearing patterned and colorful clothes, carrying sharp swords, satiated with food and drink, possessing excess wealth and goods;
our_english: Wearing ornate, colorful clothes, carrying sharp swords, gorged on food and drink, possessing excess wealth and goods —

pinyin: Shì wèi dào kuā. Fēi dào yě zāi\!
literal_gloss: This is called the boasting of thieves. It is not the Tao\!
our_english: This exposes the ringleader of thieves. It is not the Tao\!

chinese: 善建者不拔，善抱者不脫，子孫以祭祀不輟。
pinyin: Shàn jiàn zhě bù bá, shàn bào zhě bù tuō, zǐ sūn yǐ jì sì bù chuò.
literal_gloss: What is masterfully established cannot be uprooted, what is masterfully embraced cannot slip away, descendants will offer sacrifices/worship without ceasing.
our_english: What is masterfully planted cannot be uprooted. / What is masterfully embraced cannot slip away.

pinyin: Xiū zhī yú shēn, qí dé nǎi zhēn;
literal_gloss: Cultivate it in the self/body, its Virtue/Power becomes true/genuine;
our_english: Descendants will never cease offering sacrifices honoring this. / Cultivate this in your body, and its integrity becomes authentic.

pinyin: Xiū zhī yú jiā, qí dé nǎi yú;
literal_gloss: Cultivate it in the family, its Virtue becomes abundant;
our_english: Cultivate this in your family, and its integrity becomes abundant.

pinyin: Xiū zhī yú xiāng, qí dé nǎi cháng;
literal_gloss: Cultivate it in the village/community, its Virtue becomes enduring/long-lasting;
our_english: Cultivate this in your community, and its integrity becomes long-lasting. / Cultivate this in your nation, and its integrity becomes bountiful.

pinyin: Xiū zhī yú bāng, qí dé nǎi fēng;
literal_gloss: Cultivate it in the state/nation, its Virtue becomes rich/bountiful;
our_english: Cultivate this in the world, and its integrity becomes universal.

pinyin: Xiū zhī yú tiān xià, qí dé nǎi pǔ.
literal_gloss: Cultivate it in the world, its Virtue becomes universal/widespread.
our_english: Therefore, observe the body through your own body. / Observe the family through your family.

pinyin: Gù yǐ shēn guān shēn, yǐ jiā guān jiā,
literal_gloss: Therefore observe the self through the self, observe the family through the family,
our_english: Observe the community through your community.

chinese: 以鄉觀鄉，以邦觀邦，以天下觀天下。
pinyin: Yǐ xiāng guān xiāng, yǐ bāng guān bāng, yǐ tiān xià guān tiān xià.
literal_gloss: observe the village through the village, observe the state through the state, observe the world through the world.
our_english: Observe the nation through your nation. / Observe the world through the world.

chinese: 吾何以知天下然哉？以此。
pinyin: Wú hé yǐ zhī tiān xià rán zāi? Yǐ cǐ.
literal_gloss: How do I know the world is thus? By this.
our_english: How do I know the world is so? By this.

pinyin: Hán dé zhī hòu, bǐ yú chì zǐ.
literal_gloss: One containing abundant Virtue/Power is comparable to a newborn infant.
our_english: A person with abundant integrity is like a newborn. / Venomous creatures do not sting them,

chinese: 毒蟲不螫，猛獸不據，攫鳥不搏。
pinyin: Dú chóng bù shì, měng shòu bù jù, jué niǎo bù bó.
literal_gloss: Poisonous insects do not sting them, fierce beasts do not seize them, birds of prey do not strike them.
our_english: fierce beasts do not seize them, / birds of prey do not attack them.

pinyin: Gǔ ruò jīn róu ér wò gù.
literal_gloss: Bones are weak, muscles are soft, yet their grasp is firm.
our_english: Their bones are yielding and their muscles soft, yet their grip is firm.

chinese: 未知牝牡之合而朘作，精之至也。
pinyin: Wèi zhī pìn mǔ zhī hé ér zuī zuò, jīng zhī zhì yě.
literal_gloss: They do not yet know the union of male and female, yet their organ is aroused, this is the perfection/extreme of vital essence (jing).
our_english: They do not yet know the union of female and male, yet their whole being quickens with life — this is vital essence at its utmost. / It cries all day and never goes hoarse — this is harmony at its utmost.

chinese: 終日號而不嗄，和之至也。
pinyin: Zhōng rì háo ér bù shà, hé zhī zhì yě.
literal_gloss: Crying all day yet their voice does not grow hoarse, this is the perfection/extreme of harmony.
our_english: Knowing harmony is called the ever-present. / Knowing the ever-present is called clear-seeing.

pinyin: Zhī hé yuē cháng, zhī cháng yuē míng.
literal_gloss: Knowing harmony is called the constant, knowing the constant is called clarity/illumination.
our_english: To force life to increase is an ill omen.

pinyin: Yì shēng yuē xiáng. Xīn shǐ qì yuē qiáng.
literal_gloss: Artificially increasing life is called an ill omen. The mind directing the vital breath (qi) is called forcing/brute strength.
our_english: When the heart drives the vital energy, that is called strong. / When things reach their prime, they decay.

chinese: 物壯則老，謂之不道，不道早已。
pinyin: Wù zhuàng zé lǎo, wèi zhī bù dào, bù dào zǎo yǐ.
literal_gloss: When things reach peak strength they decay, this is called not-Tao, not-Tao ends early.
our_english: This is called not-Tao. Not-Tao comes to an early end.

pinyin: Zhī zhě bù yán, yán zhě bù zhī.
literal_gloss: Those who know do not speak, those who speak do not know.
our_english: Those who know do not speak. / Those who speak do not know.

pinyin: Sè qí duì, bì qí mén,
literal_gloss: Block the openings, close the doors,
our_english: Block the openings, close the doors.

pinyin: Cuò qí ruì, jiě qí fēn,
literal_gloss: Blunt the sharpness, untangle the knots/confusion,
our_english: Blunt the sharpness, untangle the knots.

pinyin: Hé qí guāng, tóng qí chén,
literal_gloss: Harmonize the light, merge with the dust;
our_english: Dim your own light, be the same as the dust.

pinyin: Shì wèi xuán tóng.
literal_gloss: This is called Profound/Mysterious Identity (Xuan Tong).
our_english: This is called profound sameness.

chinese: 故不可得而親，不可得而疏；
pinyin: Gù bù kě dé ér qīn, bù kě dé ér shū;
literal_gloss: Therefore, one cannot get close to it/them, nor can one get distant from it/them;
our_english: You cannot draw them near nor hold them off,

chinese: 不可得而利，不可得而害；
pinyin: Bù kě dé ér lì, bù kě dé ér hài;
literal_gloss: One cannot benefit it/them, nor can one harm it/them;
our_english: neither benefit nor harm them,

chinese: 不可得而貴，不可得而賤。
pinyin: Bù kě dé ér guì, bù kě dé ér jiàn.
literal_gloss: One cannot value/ennoble it/them, nor can one debase it/them.
our_english: neither honor nor debase them.

pinyin: Gù wéi tiān xià guì.
literal_gloss: Therefore they become the most valued under heaven.
our_english: And so, they become the most honored in the world.

pinyin: Yǐ zhèng zhì guó,
literal_gloss: Use correctness/orthodox to govern the state,
our_english: Govern the state with uprightness,

pinyin: yǐ jī yòng bīng,
literal_gloss: use surprise/unorthodox to deploy the military,
our_english: wage war with surprise,

pinyin: yǐ wú shì qǔ tiān xià.
literal_gloss: use non-interference (wu shi) to take/master the world.
our_english: and win the world by not meddling.

pinyin: Wú hé yǐ zhī qí rán zāi? Yǐ cǐ:
literal_gloss: How do I know it is so? By this:
our_english: How do I know it is so? By this:

pinyin: Tiān xià duō jì huì, ér mín mí pín;
literal_gloss: The more taboos/restrictions in the world, the poorer the people become;
our_english: The more taboos in the world, the poorer the people become.

pinyin: Rén duō lì qì, guó jiā zī hūn;
literal_gloss: The more sharp weapons/tools the people have, the darker/more chaotic the state becomes;
our_english: The more sharp weapons the people have, the more clouded the state becomes.

pinyin: Rén duō jì qiǎo, jī wù zī qǐ;
literal_gloss: The more skill/cunning the people have, the more strange things arise;
our_english: The more cunning people become, the more strange contrivances appear.

pinyin: Fǎ lìng zī zhāng, dào zéi duō yǒu.
literal_gloss: The more laws and decrees are made prominent, the more thieves and robbers there are.
our_english: The more laws are proclaimed, the more thieves there are.

pinyin: Gù shèng rén yún:
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage says:
our_english: Therefore the sage says:

pinyin: Wǒ wú wéi, ér mín zì huà;
literal_gloss: I execute zero-friction (wu wei), and the people transform themselves;
our_english: I do not do, and the people transform themselves.

pinyin: Wǒ hào jìng, ér mín zì zhèng;
literal_gloss: I love stillness, and the people correct themselves;
our_english: I love stillness, and the people right themselves.

pinyin: Wǒ wú shì, ér mín zì fù;
literal_gloss: I do not interfere (wu shi), and the people enrich themselves;
our_english: I do not meddle, and the people enrich themselves.

pinyin: Wǒ wú yù, ér mín zì pǔ.
literal_gloss: I have no desires, and the people return to the uncarved wood (pu) themselves.
our_english: I am desireless, and the people become plain of themselves.

pinyin: Qí zhèng mèn mèn, qí mín chún chún;
literal_gloss: When the government is dull/unobtrusive, the people are pure/honest;
our_english: When the government is dull and undiscerning, the people are pure and honest.

pinyin: Qí zhèng chá chá, qí mín quē quē.
literal_gloss: When the government is sharp/scrutinizing, the people are lacking/crafty.
our_english: When the government is sharp and prying, the people turn cunning.

pinyin: Huò xī fú zhī suǒ yǐ,
literal_gloss: Disaster is what fortune leans on,
our_english: Disaster is what fortune leans on;

pinyin: Fú xī huò zhī suǒ fú.
literal_gloss: Fortune is where disaster hides.
our_english: fortune is where disaster hides.

pinyin: Shú zhī qí jí? Qí wú zhèng.
literal_gloss: Who knows the limit/endpoint? There is no fixed norm/correctness.
our_english: Who knows where it ends? It has no fixed norm —

pinyin: Zhèng fù wéi jī, shàn fù wéi yāo.
literal_gloss: The orthodox reverts to the unorthodox, the good reverts to the monstrous.
our_english: The straight turns crooked, the good turns monstrous.

pinyin: Rén zhī mí, qí rì gù jiǔ.
literal_gloss: The delusion of people has lasted for a very long time.
our_english: People have been lost in this for a very long time.

pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén fāng ér bù gē,
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage is square but does not cut,
our_english: Therefore the sage is square but does not cut,

pinyin: lián ér bù guì,
literal_gloss: Sharp/cornered but does not injure,
our_english: sharp but does not wound,

pinyin: zhí ér bù sì,
literal_gloss: Straight but does not overreach/extend recklessly,
our_english: straight but does not overreach,

pinyin: guāng ér bù yào.
literal_gloss: Luminous but does not blind/dazzle.
our_english: bright but does not dazzle.

pinyin: Zhì rén shì tiān, mò ruò sè.
literal_gloss: In governing people and serving heaven, there is nothing like frugality/conservation.
our_english: When governing people and serving nature, nothing compares to conserving.

pinyin: Fú wéi sè, shì wèi zǎo fú;
literal_gloss: Only through frugality, is it called submitting early;
our_english: Conserving is called returning early,

pinyin: Zǎo fú wèi zhī zhòng jī dé;
literal_gloss: Submitting early is called heavily accumulating Virtue/Power (Te);
our_english: returning early is called a heavy accumulation of integrity,

pinyin: Zhòng jī dé zé wú bù kè;
literal_gloss: Heavily accumulating Virtue, there is nothing that cannot be overcome;
our_english: a heavy accumulation of integrity is when nothing cannot be overcome,

pinyin: Wú bù kè zé mò zhī qí jí;
literal_gloss: When nothing cannot be overcome, no one knows its limit;
our_english: when nothing cannot be overcome, no one knows its limit,

pinyin: Mò zhī qí jí, kě yǐ yǒu guó;
literal_gloss: When no one knows its limit, one can possess/maintain the state;
our_english: when no one knows its limit, you can have the state.

pinyin: Yǒu guó zhī mǔ, kě yǐ cháng jiǔ.
literal_gloss: Possessing the mother of the state, one can endure long.
our_english: Have the mother of the state, and you can last long.

chinese: 是謂深根固柢，長生久視之道。
pinyin: Shì wèi shēn gēn gù dǐ, cháng shēng jiǔ shì zhī dào.
literal_gloss: This is called the Tao of deep roots and firm base, of long life and enduring vision.
our_english: This is called the Tao of deep roots, firm base, long life, and enduring vision.

pinyin: Zhì dà guó, ruò pēng xiǎo xiān.
literal_gloss: Governing a large state is like cooking a small fish.
our_english: Governing a large state is like cooking a small fish.

pinyin: Yǐ dào lì tiān xià, qí guǐ bù shén;
literal_gloss: Approaching the world with the Tao, its ghosts do not manifest their spirit/numinosity;
our_english: Oversee the world with the Tao, and the ghosts lose their potency,

chinese: 非其鬼不神，其神不傷人；
pinyin: Fēi qí guǐ bù shén, qí shén bù shāng rén;
literal_gloss: Not only do the ghosts not manifest their spirit, their spirit does not harm people;
our_english: not only do ghosts lose their potency, their potency causes no harm to people,

chinese: 非其神不傷人，聖人亦不傷人。
pinyin: Fēi qí shén bù shāng rén, shèng rén yì bù shāng rén.
literal_gloss: Not only does their spirit not harm people, the Sage also does not harm people.
our_english: not only does their potency do no harm, the sage, too, does no harm to people.

chinese: 夫兩不相傷，故德交歸焉。
pinyin: Fú liǎng bù xiāng shāng, gù dé jiāo guī yān.
literal_gloss: Now then, since the two do not harm each other, their Virtue/Power converges and returns to them.
our_english: And since the two do no harm to each other, their integrity converges and returns.

pinyin: Dà guó zhě xià liú,
literal_gloss: A large state is the lower current, the downstream,
our_english: The large state is the downstream flow, / the confluence of the world, the female of the world.

pinyin: tiān xià zhī jiāo, tiān xià zhī pìn.
literal_gloss: the confluence of the world, the female of the world.
our_english: The female always overcomes the male by stillness.

chinese: 牝常以靜勝牡，以靜為下。
pinyin: Pìn cháng yǐ jìng shèng mǔ, yǐ jìng wéi xià.
literal_gloss: The female animal always overcomes the male animal by stillness; by stillness she is the low one.
our_english: By stillness she is underneath.

chinese: 故大國以下小國，則取小國；
pinyin: Gù dà guó yǐ xià xiǎo guó, zé qǔ xiǎo guó;
literal_gloss: So a large state, by going below a small state, then takes the small state;
our_english: So the large state, by going below the small state, takes the small state.

chinese: 小國以下大國，則取大國。
pinyin: Xiǎo guó yǐ xià dà guó, zé qǔ dà guó.
literal_gloss: a small state, by going below a large state, then takes the large state.
our_english: The small state, by going below the large state, takes the large state. / The large state takes by going low, the small state by staying low.

pinyin: Gù huò xià yǐ qǔ, huò xià ér qǔ.
literal_gloss: So the one goes low in order to take; the other goes low, and takes.
our_english: The large state wants nothing more than to gather and rear people.

pinyin: Dà guó bù guò yù jiān xù rén,
literal_gloss: A large state wants no more than to gather together and rear people,
our_english: The small state wants nothing more than to enter and serve people.

pinyin: Xiǎo guó bù guò yù rù shì rén.
literal_gloss: a small state wants no more than to enter and serve people.
our_english: Both get what they want.

chinese: 夫兩者各得所欲，大者宜為下。
pinyin: Fú liǎng zhě gè dé suǒ yù, dà zhě yí wéi xià.
literal_gloss: Now, the two each get what they want; the large one ought to be the low one.
our_english: The large one ought to be underneath.

pinyin: Dào zhě wàn wù zhī ào.
literal_gloss: The Tao is the ao of the countless things — the southwest corner of a dwelling, the household's altar space and place of honor.
our_english: The Tao is the sanctuary of the countless things, / the treasure of those who are masterful,

chinese: 善人之寶，不善人之所保。
pinyin: Shàn rén zhī bǎo, bù shàn rén zhī suǒ bǎo.
literal_gloss: The treasure (bao) of the masterful person, the safekeeping (bao) of the unmasterful person.
our_english: and what keeps safe those who are not.

chinese: 美言可以市尊，美行可以加人。
pinyin: Měi yán kě yǐ shì zūn, měi xíng kě yǐ jiā rén.
literal_gloss: Fine words can buy (shi — market, trade for) honor; fine conduct can raise a person above others. (The silks and both commentators split after 市 — see notes/manuscript.md.)
our_english: Fine words can buy honor.

pinyin: Rén zhī bù shàn, hé qì zhī yǒu?
literal_gloss: As for a person's being unmasterful — what abandoning (qi) of them is there? (he...zhi you: a fixed idiom, "what X is there?" = there is none.)
our_english: Fine conduct can raise a person above others. / So when a person is unmasterful, why abandon them?

pinyin: Gù lì tiān zǐ, zhì sān gōng,
literal_gloss: So when they raise up (li — to stand a thing upright) a child of the sky (tian zi) and install the three gong,
our_english: When they raise up a child of the sky and install the three ministers,

pinyin: Suī yǒu gǒng bì yǐ xiān sì mǎ,
literal_gloss: though there are jade discs too wide for one pair of arms, borne ahead of a team of four horses,
our_english: though jade discs go before teams of four horses,

pinyin: Bù rú zuò jìn cǐ dào.
literal_gloss: it is not as good as sitting still and offering this Tao.
our_english: better to sit where you are and offer this Tao. / What made the ancients honor this Tao?

pinyin: Gǔ zhī suǒ yǐ guì cǐ dào zhě hé?
literal_gloss: What made the ancients honor this Tao?
our_english: Did they not say: seek, and you find;

chinese: 不曰：求以得，有罪以免邪？
pinyin: Bù yuē: qiú yǐ dé, yǒu zuì yǐ miǎn xié?
literal_gloss: Did they not say: seek, and you find; have a crime (zui) against you, and you are spared?
our_english: commit a crime, and you are spared?

pinyin: Gù wéi tiān xià guì.
literal_gloss: And so it is the most honored in the world.
our_english: And so it is the most honored in the world.

pinyin: Wéi wú wéi, shì wú shì, wèi wú wèi.
literal_gloss: Do the not-doing, serve the not-serving, taste the flavorless. (Each beat is one character twice, with wu — no — between.)
our_english: Do the not-doing, / serve the not-serving,

pinyin: Dà xiǎo duō shǎo, bào yuàn yǐ dé.
literal_gloss: Great, small, many, few; repay resentment with integrity (de).
our_english: taste the flavorless. / Great or small, many or few,

chinese: 圖難於其易，為大於其細。
pinyin: Tú nán yú qí yì, wéi dà yú qí xì.
literal_gloss: Map out the difficult while it is easy; do the great while it is slight (xi — thread-fine).
our_english: repay resentment with integrity. / Map out the difficult while it is easy.

pinyin: Tiān xià nán shì, bì zuò yú yì;
literal_gloss: The world's difficult affairs always arise from the easy;
our_english: Do the great while it is slight. / The world's difficult affairs always begin easy.

pinyin: Tiān xià dà shì, bì zuò yú xì.
literal_gloss: the world's great affairs always arise from the slight.
our_english: The world's great affairs always begin slight. / So the sage never does the great,

chinese: 是以聖人終不為大，故能成其大。
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén zhōng bù wéi dà, gù néng chéng qí dà.
literal_gloss: Therefore the sage to the end never does the great, and so can complete their greatness.
our_english: and so completes their greatness. / Promise lightly and you will be little trusted.

chinese: 夫輕諾必寡信，多易必多難。
pinyin: Fú qīng nuò bì guǎ xìn, duō yì bì duō nán.
literal_gloss: Now, a light promise inevitably means scant trust (xin); taking much to be easy inevitably means much difficulty.
our_english: Take much to be easy and much will be difficult. / So the sage still finds it difficult,

chinese: 是以聖人猶難之，故終無難矣。
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén yóu nán zhī, gù zhōng wú nán yǐ.
literal_gloss: Therefore the sage still treats them as difficult, and so to the end has no difficulty.
our_english: and in the end has no difficulty.

pinyin: Qí ān yì chí, qí wèi zhào yì móu.
literal_gloss: What is at rest/stable is easy to hold, what has not yet shown signs is easy to plan for.
our_english: What is at rest is easy to hold. / What shows no sign is easy to plan for.

pinyin: Qí cuì yì pàn, qí wēi yì sàn.
literal_gloss: What is brittle is easy to break/melt, what is microscopic/subtle is easy to scatter.
our_english: What is brittle is easy to shatter. / What is faint is easy to scatter.

chinese: 為之於未有，治之於未亂。
pinyin: Wéi zhī yú wèi yǒu, zhì zhī yú wèi luàn.
literal_gloss: Execute it before it exists, govern/order it before it is chaotic.
our_english: Handle it before it exists. / Order it before it falls into disorder.

pinyin: Hé bào zhī mù, shēng yú háo mò;
literal_gloss: A tree you can wrap your arms around grows from a tiny sprout;
our_english: The tree the width of both arms is born from a hair's tip.

pinyin: Jiǔ céng zhī tái, qǐ yú lěi tǔ;
literal_gloss: A nine-story terrace begins with a pile of dirt;
our_english: The nine-tiered terrace rises from a heap of dirt. / The thousand-mile journey begins beneath your feet.

pinyin: Qiān lǐ zhī xíng, shǐ yú zú xià.
literal_gloss: A journey of a thousand miles begins beneath the feet.
our_english: Those who handle it ruin it. / Those who grasp it lose it.

pinyin: Wéi zhě bài zhī, zhí zhě shī zhī.
literal_gloss: Those who force/act ruin it, those who grasp/hold lose it.
our_english: Therefore, the sage does not do, and so ruins nothing,

chinese: 是以聖人無為故無敗，無執故無失。
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén wú wéi gù wú bài, wú zhí gù wú shī.
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage executes zero-friction (wu wei) thus has no ruin, grasps nothing thus has no loss.
our_english: does not grasp, and so loses nothing. / People often ruin their affairs just short of completing them.

chinese: 民之從事，常於幾成而敗之。
pinyin: Mín zhī cóng shì, cháng yú jī chéng ér bài zhī.
literal_gloss: People handling affairs, often ruin them when they are near compilation/completion (cheng).
our_english: Be as careful at the end as at the beginning, / and nothing will be ruined.

pinyin: Shèn zhōng rú shǐ, zé wú bài shì.
literal_gloss: Be careful at the end as at the beginning, then there will be no ruined affairs.
our_english: Therefore, the sage wants the not-wanting

chinese: 是以聖人欲不欲，不貴難得之貨；
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén yù bù yù, bù guì nán dé zhī huò;
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage desires to not desire, does not value hard-to-obtain goods;
our_english: and does not prize rare goods, / learns to unlearn,

pinyin: Xué bù xué, fù zhòng rén zhī suǒ guò.
literal_gloss: Learns what is unlearned, reverts/returns what the multitudes have passed by.
our_english: brings the crowd back from where they have gone too far, / and supports the countless things in being so of themselves,

chinese: 以輔萬物之自然，而不敢為。
pinyin: Yǐ fǔ wàn wù zhī zì rán, ér bù gǎn wéi.
literal_gloss: In order to assist the spontaneous autonomy (zi ran) of the ten thousand things, and does not dare to force/execute (wei).
our_english: and never pushes them.

chinese: 古之善為道者，非以明民，將以愚之。
pinyin: Gǔ zhī shàn wéi dào zhě, fēi yǐ míng mín, jiāng yǐ yú zhī.
literal_gloss: The ancients who were masterful at executing the Tao, did not use it to enlighten the people, but to keep them unformatted/simple (yu).
our_english: The ancients who were masterful at the Tao / did not use it to make the people clever.

pinyin: Mín zhī nán zhì, yǐ qí zhì duō.
literal_gloss: The people are difficult to govern, because their cunning/cleverness (zhi) is excessive.
our_english: They used it to return them to being guileless. / The people are hard to govern

pinyin: Gù yǐ zhì zhì guó, guó zhī zéi;
literal_gloss: Therefore, using cunning/cleverness to govern the state is a thief to the state;
our_english: because they have too much guile. / So to govern a state with guile robs the state.

pinyin: Bù yǐ zhì zhì guó, guó zhī fú.
literal_gloss: Not using cunning/cleverness to govern the state is a blessing to the state.
our_english: Not to govern it with guile is the state's good fortune. / Knowing these two is itself the pattern.

pinyin: Zhī cǐ liǎng zhě yì jī shì.
literal_gloss: Knowing these two is also the absolute standard/pattern.
our_english: Always to know the pattern / is called profound integrity.

pinyin: Cháng zhī jī shì, shì wèi xuán dé.
literal_gloss: Always knowing the absolute standard/pattern, this is called Profound Virtue (Te).
our_english: Profound integrity is deep, and far, / and turns back together with things,

chinese: 玄德深矣，遠矣，與物反矣，然後乃至大順。
pinyin: Xuán dé shēn yǐ, yuǎn yǐ, yǔ wù fǎn yǐ, rán hòu nǎi zhì dà shùn.
literal_gloss: Profound Virtue is deep, is far-reaching, it reverts/returns with physical entities (wu), and only then reaches the Great Harmony/Smoothness.
our_english: and only then runs with the great current.

chinese: 江海所以能為百谷王者，
pinyin: Jiāng hǎi suǒ yǐ néng wéi bǎi gǔ wáng zhě,
literal_gloss: The reason rivers and seas can function as the kings of the hundred valleys,
our_english: Rivers and seas can rule the hundred valleys / because they are masterful at staying below them.

chinese: 以其善下之，故能為百谷王。
pinyin: Yǐ qí shàn xià zhī, gù néng wéi bǎi gǔ wáng.
literal_gloss: Is because they are masterful at positioning themselves lower than them, thus they can function as the kings of the hundred valleys.
our_english: That is how they come to rule the hundred valleys.

chinese: 是以欲上民，必以言下之；
pinyin: Shì yǐ yù shàng mín, bì yǐ yán xià zhī;
literal_gloss: Therefore, wishing to be above the people, one must by words position oneself below them;
our_english: So to rise above the people, you must speak from below them.

pinyin: Yù xiān mín, bì yǐ shēn hòu zhī.
literal_gloss: Wishing to be ahead of the people, one must put one's person/body behind them.
our_english: To walk ahead of the people, you must put your body behind them.

chinese: 是以聖人處上而民不重，
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén chǔ shàng ér mín bù zhòng,
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage dwells above and the people do not feel heavy/burdened;
our_english: The sage stands above, and the people are not weighed down, / stands in front, and the people are not hindered.

pinyin: Chǔ qián ér mín bù hài.
literal_gloss: Dwells in front and the people do not feel harmed/obstructed.
our_english: So the world gladly pushes them forward and never tires of them.

pinyin: Shì yǐ tiān xià lè tuī ér bù yàn.
literal_gloss: Therefore the world gladly pushes them forward and does not tire of them.
our_english: Because they do not contend,

chinese: 以其不爭，故天下莫能與之爭。
pinyin: Yǐ qí bù zhēng, gù tiān xià mò néng yǔ zhī zhēng.
literal_gloss: Because they do not compete/contend, therefore no one in the world can compete with them.
our_english: no one in the world can contend with them.

chinese: 天下皆謂我道大，似不肖。
pinyin: Tiān xià jiē wèi wǒ dào dà, sì bù xiào.
literal_gloss: The whole world says my Tao is great, but seems unlike/unworthy (of comparison).
our_english: Everyone says my Tao is great, and looks like nothing. / Only because it is great does it look like nothing.

pinyin: Fú wéi dà, gù sì bù xiào.
literal_gloss: Because it is great, therefore it seems unlike.
our_english: If it looked like anything, it would long since have been slight.

pinyin: Ruò xiào, jiǔ yǐ qí xì yě fú\!
literal_gloss: If it were like (others), for a long time it would have been small/insignificant\!
our_english: I have three treasures. I hold them and keep them safe. / The first is tenderness.

pinyin: Wǒ yǒu sān bǎo, chí ér bǎo zhī:
literal_gloss: I have three treasures, holding and guarding them:
our_english: The second is frugality.

chinese: 一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先。
pinyin: Yī yuē cí, èr yuē jiǎn, sān yuē bù gǎn wéi tiān xià xiān.
literal_gloss: The first is called compassion/deep love, the second is called frugality/conservation, the third is called not daring to function as the first/ahead of the world.
our_english: The third is never pushing to be first in the world. / Tenderness, and so you can be brave.

pinyin: Cí gù néng yǒng;
literal_gloss: Compassion, thus able to be brave;
our_english: Frugality, and so you can reach far.

pinyin: Jiǎn gù néng guǎng;
literal_gloss: Frugality, thus able to be broad/expansive;
our_english: Never pushing to be first in the world, and so you can become chief of the vessels. / Now: to abandon tenderness and grab at courage,

chinese: 不敢為天下先，故能成器長。
pinyin: Bù gǎn wéi tiān xià xiān, gù néng chéng qì zhǎng.
literal_gloss: Not daring to be first in the world, thus able to compile/complete as the chief of tools/vessels.
our_english: to abandon frugality and grab at reach,

chinese: 今捨慈且勇，捨儉且廣，捨後且先，死矣！
pinyin: Jīn shě cí qiě yǒng, shě jiǎn qiě guǎng, shě hòu qiě xiān, sǐ yǐ\!
literal_gloss: Now to abandon compassion and just be brave, to abandon frugality and just be expansive, to abandon the rear and just be first, is death\!
our_english: to abandon the rear and grab at the front. / That is death.

chinese: 夫慈，以戰則勝，以守則固。
pinyin: Fú cí, yǐ zhàn zé shèng, yǐ shǒu zé gù.
literal_gloss: Now compassion, used in battle it wins, used in defense it is solid/firm.
our_english: Tenderness. Fight with it and you win, guard with it and you stand firm.

pinyin: Tiān jiāng jiù zhī, yǐ cí wèi zhī.
literal_gloss: Heaven will save/rescue them, using compassion to guard them.
our_english: When nature would rescue someone, it shields them with tenderness.

pinyin: Shàn wéi shì zhě, bù wǔ;
literal_gloss: A masterful warrior/scholar is not martial/violent;
our_english: Those masterful in service are not martial.

pinyin: Shàn zhàn zhě, bù nù;
literal_gloss: A masterful fighter does not become angry;
our_english: The master fighter does not rage.

pinyin: Shàn shèng dí zhě, bù yǔ;
literal_gloss: A masterful conqueror of enemies does not engage/contend with them;
our_english: The master of overcoming enemies does not engage them.

pinyin: Shàn yòng rén zhě, wéi zhī xià.
literal_gloss: A masterful user of people functions as their subordinate/lower.
our_english: The master of using people puts themselves below them.

pinyin: Shì wèi bù zhēng zhī dé,
literal_gloss: This is called the Virtue/Power (Te) of not competing/contending,
our_english: This is called the integrity of not contending.

pinyin: Shì wèi yòng rén zhī lì,
literal_gloss: This is called the ability/power to use people,
our_english: This is called using people's force.

pinyin: Shì wèi pèi tiān, gǔ zhī jí.
literal_gloss: This is called matching/pairing with Heaven, the ultimate of antiquity.
our_english: This is called partnered with the sky, the pinnacle of the ancients.

pinyin: Yòng bīng yǒu yán:
literal_gloss: Deploying the military has a saying:
our_english: Soldiers have a saying:

pinyin: Wú bù gǎn wéi zhǔ, ér wéi kè;
literal_gloss: I dare not function as the host/initiator, but function as the guest/responder;
our_english: I do not push to move first. I move second.

pinyin: Bù gǎn jìn cùn, ér tuì chǐ.
literal_gloss: Dare not advance an inch, but retreat a foot.
our_english: I do not push an inch into another's ground. I give up a foot of my own.

pinyin: Shì wèi xíng wú xíng,
literal_gloss: This is called marching without marching,
our_english: This is called marching where there are no ranks,

pinyin: Rǎng wú bì,
literal_gloss: Rolling up sleeves without arms,
our_english: baring an arm where there is no arm,

pinyin: Rēng wú dí,
literal_gloss: Grasping without an enemy,
our_english: hauling where there is no enemy,

pinyin: Zhí wú bīng.
literal_gloss: Holding without weapons.
our_english: grasping where there is no weapon.

pinyin: Huò mò dà yú qīng dí,
literal_gloss: There is no disaster greater than treating the enemy as weightless/light;
our_english: There is no disaster greater than making light of the enemy.

pinyin: Qīng dí jī sàng wú bǎo.
literal_gloss: Treating the enemy as weightless almost destroys my treasures.
our_english: Making light of the enemy nearly costs me my treasures.

pinyin: Gù kàng bīng xiāng ruò, āi zhě shèng yǐ.
literal_gloss: Therefore when opposing troops meet/match, the grieving/sorrowful one wins.
our_english: Therefore, when the armies are evenly matched, the side that grieves wins.

pinyin: Wú yán shèn yì zhī, shèn yì xíng.
literal_gloss: My words are very easy to understand, very easy to execute.
our_english: My words are very easy to know, / very easy to follow.

pinyin: Tiān xià mò néng zhī, mò néng xíng.
literal_gloss: No one in the world can understand them, no one can execute them.
our_english: In all the world, no one can know them. / No one can follow them.

pinyin: Yán yǒu zōng, shì yǒu jūn.
literal_gloss: Words have an ancestor/root, affairs have a sovereign/master.
our_english: Words have an ancestor. / Affairs have a ruler.

pinyin: Fú wéi wú zhī, shì yǐ bù wǒ zhī.
literal_gloss: Precisely because they lack understanding, therefore they do not understand me.
our_english: Only because there is no knowing it, / they do not know me.

pinyin: Zhī wǒ zhě xī, zé wǒ zhě guì.
literal_gloss: Those who understand me are rare, those who follow/model me are valued.
our_english: Those who know me are few. / Those who pattern themselves on me are precious.

pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén pī hè ér huái yù.
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage wears coarse clothes but carries jade in their bosom.
our_english: Therefore, the sage wears coarse cloth, but carries jade against their chest.

pinyin: Zhī bù zhī, shàng;
literal_gloss: Knowing that one does not know, is superior/highest;
our_english: To know you do not know is highest.

pinyin: Bù zhī zhī, bìng.
literal_gloss: Not knowing yet thinking one knows, is a disease/flaw.
our_english: To not know yet claim to know is sickness.

pinyin: Fú wéi bìng bìng, shì yǐ bù bìng.
literal_gloss: Only by recognizing the disease as a disease, therefore one is not diseased.
our_english: Only when you are sick of the sickness are you not sick.

chinese: 聖人不病，以其病病，是以不病。
pinyin: Shèng rén bù bìng, yǐ qí bìng bìng, shì yǐ bù bìng.
literal_gloss: The Sage is not diseased, because they recognize the disease as a disease, therefore they are not diseased.
our_english: The sage is not sick because they are sick of the sickness.

pinyin: Mín bù wèi wēi, zé dà wēi zhì.
literal_gloss: When the people do not fear authority/might, then great authority/might arrives.
our_english: When the people no longer fear authority, / the great collapse comes.

chinese: 無狎其所居，無厭其所生。
pinyin: Wú xiá qí suǒ jū, wú yàn qí suǒ shēng.
literal_gloss: Do not crowd/harass their place of residence, do not oppress/weary their livelihood.
our_english: Do not crowd people in their homes.

pinyin: Fú wéi bù yàn, shì yǐ bù yàn.
literal_gloss: Precisely because one does not oppress them, therefore they do not find it oppressive.
our_english: Do not oppress their livelihoods.

pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén zì zhī, bù zì jiàn;
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage knows self, but does not display self;
our_english: Only when you do not oppress them will they not tire of you. / And so the sage knows themselves and does not display themselves,

pinyin: Zì ài, bù zì guì.
literal_gloss: Loves self, but does not esteem/exalt self.
our_english: loves themselves and does not hold themselves precious.

pinyin: Gù qù bǐ qǔ cǐ.
literal_gloss: Therefore discard that and choose this.
our_english: They let go of what is out there and take what is here.

pinyin: Yǒng yú gǎn zé shā,
literal_gloss: Brave in daring, then (one) gets killed;
our_english: Bravery in pushing gets you killed. / Bravery in not pushing keeps you alive.

pinyin: Yǒng yú bù gǎn zé huó.
literal_gloss: Brave in not daring, then (one) lives.
our_english: Of these two, one benefits and one harms.

pinyin: Cǐ liǎng zhě, huò lì huò hài.
literal_gloss: These two things, one is beneficial, one is harmful.
our_english: What nature turns against, who knows why?

pinyin: Tiān zhī suǒ wù, shú zhī qí gù?
literal_gloss: That which Heaven dislikes, who knows the reason/cause?
our_english: So the sage still finds it difficult.

pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén yóu nán zhī.
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage still treats it as difficult.
our_english: The way of nature:

pinyin: Tiān zhī dào, bù zhēng ér shàn shèng,
literal_gloss: The Tao of Heaven: does not contend yet masterfully conquers,
our_english: it does not contend, yet is masterful at overcoming. / It does not speak, yet is masterful at answering.

pinyin: Bù yán ér shàn yìng,
literal_gloss: Does not speak yet masterfully responds,
our_english: It does not summon, yet things come of themselves.

pinyin: Bù zhào ér zì lái,
literal_gloss: Does not summon yet it comes by itself,
our_english: It is unhurried, yet masterful at planning.

pinyin: Chǎn rán ér shàn móu.
literal_gloss: It is loose/spacious yet masterfully plans.
our_english: Nature's net is vast.

pinyin: Tiān wǎng huī huī, shū ér bù shī.
literal_gloss: Heaven's net is vast/broad, wide-meshed yet nothing escapes.
our_english: Its mesh is wide, and nothing slips through.

chinese: 民不畏死，奈何以死懼之？
pinyin: Mín bù wèi sǐ, nài hé yǐ sǐ jù zhī?
literal_gloss: When the people do not fear death, why use death to threaten them?
our_english: When the people do not fear death, / why try to frighten them with death?

chinese: 若使民常畏死，而為奇者，吾得執而殺之，孰敢？
pinyin: Ruò shǐ mín cháng wèi sǐ, ér wéi qí zhě, wú dé zhí ér shā zhī, shú gǎn?
literal_gloss: If you make the people constantly fear death, and those who perform odd/illegal acts, I can seize and kill them—who would dare?
our_english: Suppose the people always feared death, / and I could seize whoever steps out of line and kill them.

pinyin: Cháng yǒu sī shā zhě shā.
literal_gloss: There is always a Master of Killing who kills.
our_english: Who would still push? / There is always one who does the killing.

chinese: 夫代司殺者殺，是謂代大匠斫。
pinyin: Fú dài sī shā zhě shā, shì wèi dài dà jiàng zhuó.
literal_gloss: Now to take the place of the Master of Killing to kill, is called taking the place of the Great Carpenter to hew.
our_english: To take their place is to take the place of the master carpenter. / Of those who carve in place of the master carpenter,

chinese: 夫代大匠斫，希有不傷其手矣。
pinyin: Fú dài dà jiàng zhuó, xī yǒu bù shāng qí shǒu yǐ.
literal_gloss: To take the place of the Great Carpenter to hew, rarely is there anyone who does not injure their own hand.
our_english: few fail to cut their own hand.

chinese: 民之飢，以其上食稅之多，是以飢。
pinyin: Mín zhī jī, yǐ qí shàng shí shuì zhī duō, shì yǐ jī.
literal_gloss: The hunger of the people, because their superiors consume taxes in such quantity, therefore they are hungry.
our_english: The people go hungry / because those over them eat up so much in taxes.

chinese: 民之難治，以其上之有為，是以難治。
pinyin: Mín zhī nán zhì, yǐ qí shàng zhī yǒu wéi, shì yǐ nán zhì.
literal_gloss: The people are difficult to govern, because their superiors have "doing" (interference), therefore they are difficult to govern.
our_english: The people are hard to govern / because those over them will not stop doing.

chinese: 民之輕死，以其上求生之厚，是以輕死。
pinyin: Mín zhī qīng sǐ, yǐ qí shàng qiú shēng zhī hòu, shì yǐ qīng sǐ.
literal_gloss: The people treat death lightly, because their superiors seek "life" (luxury) with such thickness/profuseness, therefore they treat death lightly.
our_english: The people make light of death / because those over them want their own lives so rich.

chinese: 夫唯無以生為者，是賢於貴生。
pinyin: Fú wéi wú yǐ shēng wéi zhě, shì xián yú guì shēng.
literal_gloss: Only those who do not use "living" as a "doing," are worthier than those who value/prize life.
our_english: Those who don't use living for doing / are worthier than those who hold life precious.

chinese: 人之生也柔弱，其死也堅強。
pinyin: Rén zhī shēng yě róu ruò, qí sǐ yě jiān qiáng.
literal_gloss: Human life is supple/soft and weak; at death it is rigid and hard/strong.
our_english: In life a person is soft and yielding. / In death, hard and strong.

chinese: 萬物草木之生也柔脆，其死也枯槁。
pinyin: Wàn wù cǎo mù zhī shēng yě róu cuì, qí sǐ yě kū gǎo.
literal_gloss: The ten thousand things—grass and trees—are in life supple and fragile; at death they are withered and dried.
our_english: In life the countless things, the grasses and trees, are soft and tender. / In death, withered and dry.

pinyin: Gù jiān qiáng zhě sǐ zhī tú,
literal_gloss: Therefore the rigid and hard/strong are the disciples/company of death,
our_english: So the hard and strong are followers of death.

pinyin: Róu ruò zhě shēng zhī tú.
literal_gloss: The supple and weak are the disciples/company of life.
our_english: The soft and yielding are followers of life. / This is why a strong army does not win,

chinese: 是以兵強則不勝，木強則折。
pinyin: Shì yǐ bīng qiáng zé bù shèng, mù qiáng zé zhé.
literal_gloss: Therefore, if troops are hard/strong, they will not win; if a tree is hard/strong, it will snap.
our_english: and a strong tree snaps. / The strong and the big dwell below.

pinyin: Qiáng dà chǔ xià, róu ruò chǔ shàng.
literal_gloss: The hard/strong and big reside below, the supple and weak reside above.
our_english: The soft and the yielding dwell above.

pinyin: Tiān zhī dào, qí yóu zhāng gōng yǔ?
literal_gloss: The Tao of Heaven, is it not like drawing a bow?
our_english: The way of nature: / is it not like stringing a bow? / The high is pressed down, the low is lifted.

pinyin: Gāo zhě yì zhī, xià zhě jǔ zhī;
literal_gloss: The high is lowered, the low is raised;
our_english: What is too much is drawn off. What is too little is filled in. / The way of nature

chinese: 有餘者損之，不足者補之。
pinyin: Yǒu yú zhě sǔn zhī, bù zú zhě bǔ zhī.
literal_gloss: Those who have excess, it diminishes; those who are insufficient, it supplements.
our_english: takes from where there is too much / and mends where there is too little.

chinese: 天之道，損有餘而補不足。
pinyin: Tiān zhī dào, sǔn yǒu yú ér bǔ bù zú.
literal_gloss: The Tao of Heaven: diminishes those who have excess and supplements those who are insufficient.
our_english: The way of people is not like this. / It takes from those who have too little / and offers it up to those who have too much.

chinese: 人之道，則不然，損不足以奉有餘。
pinyin: Rén zhī dào, zé bù rán, sǔn bù zú yǐ fèng yǒu yú.
literal_gloss: The Tao of humanity is not like this: it diminishes those who are insufficient to serve those who have excess.
our_english: Who has more than enough, / and offers it up to the world?

chinese: 孰能有餘以奉天下？唯有道者。
pinyin: Shú néng yǒu yú yǐ fèng tiān xià? Wéi yǒu dào zhě.
literal_gloss: Who can have excess to serve the world? Only the one who has the Tao.
our_english: Only those who are with the Tao. / Therefore the sage acts yet relies on nothing.

chinese: 是以聖人為而不恃，功成而不處，其不欲見賢。
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén wéi ér bù shì, gōng chéng ér bù chù, qí bù yù jiàn xián.
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage acts but does not rely, accomplishes work but does not take credit; they do not wish to display their worth.
our_english: The work is done, and they do not stay in it. / They have no wish to appear exceptional.

pinyin: Tiān xià mò róu ruò yú shuǐ,
literal_gloss: In the world, nothing is more supple and weak than water,
our_english: In all the world nothing is softer and more yielding than water, / yet at attacking the hard and the strong nothing overcomes it, / for nothing can take its place.

chinese: 而攻堅強者莫之能勝，以其無以易之。
pinyin: Ér gōng jiān qiáng zhě mò zhī néng shèng, yǐ qí wú yǐ yì zhī.
literal_gloss: Yet in attacking the hard and strong, nothing can surpass it, because nothing can replace it.
our_english: The yielding overcomes the strong. / The soft overcomes the hard. / No one in the world fails to know this,

chinese: 弱之勝強，柔之勝剛，天下莫不知，莫能行。
pinyin: Ruò zhī shèng qiáng, róu zhī shèng gāng, tiān xià mò bù zhī, mò néng xíng.
literal_gloss: That the weak conquers the strong, the supple conquers the hard/rigid—the world knows this, but no one can practice it.
our_english: yet no one can follow it. / So the sage says:

chinese: 是以聖人云：受國之垢，是謂社稷主；受國之不祥，是謂天下王。
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén yún: shòu guó zhī gòu, shì wèi shè jì zhǔ; shòu guó zhī bù xiáng, shì wèi tiān xià wáng.
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage says: To accept the state's filth is to be the Lord of the Altars (the people); to accept the state's misfortune is to be the King of the World.
our_english: whoever takes on the filth of the state / is the keeper of the soil and the grain. / Whoever takes on the ill omen of the state

pinyin: Zhèng yán ruò fǎn.
literal_gloss: Right words seem like the opposite (paradoxical).
our_english: is the ruler of the world. / Words on the mark seem like their opposite.

chinese: 和大怨，必有餘怨；安可以為善？
pinyin: Hé dà yuàn, bì yǒu yú yuàn; ān kě yǐ wéi shàn?
literal_gloss: Even after reconciling a great grudge, there must remain some residual resentment; how can this be considered "good"?
our_english: Settle a great grudge / and some grudge always remains. / How could that count as masterful?

chinese: 是以聖人執左契，而不責於人。
pinyin: Shì yǐ shèng rén zhí zuǒ qì, ér bù zé yú rén.
literal_gloss: Therefore the Sage holds the left (debtor's) tally, and does not exact payment from people.
our_english: So the sage grasps the left half of the tally / and never asks for the other.

pinyin: Yǒu dé sī qì, wú dé sī chè.
literal_gloss: Those with Virtue manage the tally; those without Virtue manage the taxes/collection.
our_english: Those with integrity keep the tally. / Those without integrity keep score.

pinyin: Tiān dào wú qīn, cháng yǔ shàn rén.
literal_gloss: The Tao of Heaven has no favorites; it constantly sides with the "good" people (the natural/authentic).
our_english: The way of nature plays no favorites. / It stays with those who are masterful.

chinese: 小國寡民。使有什伯之器而不用；
pinyin: Xiǎo guó guǎ mín. Shǐ yǒu shí bǎi zhī qì ér bù yòng;
literal_gloss: A small state with few people. Let them have ten-fold and hundred-fold labor-saving devices and not use them;
our_english: A small state, few people. / Let the people have tools that do the work of ten, of a hundred, yet no need to use them. / Let the people find death heavy, and not move far away.

pinyin: Shǐ mín zhòng sǐ ér bù yuǎn xǐ.
literal_gloss: Let the people take death seriously and not move far away.
our_english: Though there are boats and carts, there is no call to travel in them. / Though there are armor and weapons, there is no call to march them out.

chinese: 雖有舟輿，無所乘之；雖有甲兵，無所陳之。
pinyin: Suī yǒu zhōu yú, wú suǒ chéng zhī; suī yǒu jiǎ bīng, wú suǒ chén zhī.
literal_gloss: Though they have boats and carriages, there is no need to ride them; though they have armor and weapons, there is no need to display them.
our_english: Let the people go back to keeping their records in knotted cord. / They find their food sweet,

pinyin: Shǐ mín fù jié shéng ér yòng zhī.
literal_gloss: Let the people go back to tying knots and using them (as their record).
our_english: their clothes fine, / their houses restful, / their ways a pleasure.

chinese: 甘其食，美其服，安其居，樂其俗。
pinyin: Gān qí shí, měi qí fú, ān qí jū, lè qí sú.
literal_gloss: Find their food sweet, find their clothing beautiful, find their dwelling peaceful, find their customs joyful.
our_english: Neighboring states lie within sight of each other. / They hear each other's chickens and dogs.

chinese: 隣國相望，雞犬之聲相聞，民至老死，不相往來。
pinyin: Lín guó xiāng wàng, jī quǎn zhī shēng xiāng wén, mín zhì lǎo sǐ, bù xiāng wǎng lái.
literal_gloss: Neighboring states look at each other, the sounds of cocks and dogs are heard across, yet the people, until they grow old and die, do not go back and forth (trade/commute).
our_english: The people grow old and die / and never once go next door.

pinyin: Xìn yán bù měi, měi yán bù xìn.
literal_gloss: Truthful words are not beautiful/decorative; beautiful/decorative words are not truthful.
our_english: Trustworthy words are not pretty. / Pretty words are not trustworthy. / Those who are masterful do not argue.

pinyin: Shàn zhě bù biàn, biàn zhě bù shàn.
literal_gloss: Those who are "good" (authentic) do not argue/debate; those who argue/debate are not "good."
our_english: Those who argue are not masterful. / Those who know have not heard it all.

pinyin: Zhī zhě bù bó, bó zhě bù zhī.
literal_gloss: Those who truly know are not broadly learned (in superficial knowledge); those who are broadly learned do not truly know.
our_english: Those who have heard it all do not know. / The sage does not hoard.

chinese: 聖人不積。既以為人己愈有，既以與人己愈多。
pinyin: Shèng rén bù jī. Jì yǐ wéi rén jǐ yù yǒu, jì yǐ yǔ rén jǐ yù duō.
literal_gloss: The Sage does not hoard. Since they do things for people, they have more for themselves; since they give to people, they have more for themselves.
our_english: Having done for others, they have more. / Having given to others, they have more still.

chinese: 天之道，利而不害；聖人之道，為而不爭。
pinyin: Tiān zhī dào, lì ér bù hài; shèng rén zhī dào, wéi ér bù zhēng.
literal_gloss: The Tao of Heaven: benefits but does not harm; the Tao of the Sage: acts but does not contend.
our_english: The way of nature benefits and does not harm. / The way of the sage acts and does not contend.
